appraisal_events.evidence: « Dire que j'ai gâché des années de ma vie, que j'ai voulu mourir, que j'ai eu mon plus grand amour, pour une femme qui ne me plaisait pas, qui n'était pas mon genre ! »
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann's inner exclamation explicitly devalues Odette as undeserving of his love, but the narrator has just framed this reaction as boorish (muflerie), undercutting the reliability of the judgment.

status_effects.explanation: Swann's callous dismissal of her as a woman who never suited him locally diminishes her, though the narrator's framing of this as boorishness tempers how much weight the judgment carries.

ambiguities: Whether Odette's devaluation in Swann's exclamation should be read as a genuine local diminishment of her, or purely as evidence of Swann's own boorishness (per the accepted annotation), is ambiguous; the narrator's irony is directed at Swann, not clearly at endorsing or rejecting his view of Odette.
